subject: Follow-up: aligning billing units, caching impact, and target $/1M
messages:
From: Alexa Moore <alexa.moore@fintechco.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up on pricing metrics from today's call

Markus / Aditya —

Thanks for the clear demo this morning. Two quick things we need to align internally before we share with procurement:

1) Billing unit confusion — our engineering team asked whether Redwood bills by tokens, characters, or requests. They referred to some old benchmark notes where characters were used for estimating costs. Which is the canonical billing unit?

2) Prompt caching impact — we have heavy shared prefixes in our flows (welcome screens, system prompts). If we cache prefixes on Redwood, do those saved prefixes reduce billed tokens for subsequent calls? Or are we still billed for the full input+output tokens?

3) Budget & target economics — rough expected usage for Q2 is ~120M tokens/month (after initial ramp). Our procurement target is to keep infra spend under $2,500/month initially. Can you help translate what $/1M tokens we should expect for that budget and whether caching would materially change the number?

I've attached the MAP draft and the recording link for reference.

Next steps from us: we can run a small tech spike next week if you can confirm where to instrument cache metrics. Procurement is waiting on a $/1M line item.

Thanks,
Alexa

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up on pricing metrics from today's call

Hi Alexa —

Great questions. Quick summary answers first, then a short worked example using your 120M/month estimate.

1) Canonical billing unit: Redwood bills usage in tokens. Characters are used internally as a rough estimator because they’re human-readable, but they are not used for billing. Requests (API calls) are not billed as a unit; cost is driven by the number of tokens processed (prompt + completion).

2) Prompt/prefix caching: caching can reduce billed tokens, but only when the cached prefix allows us to avoid re-sending token content to the model. There are two relevant cache types:
   - Client-side / prefix reuse: if you send the same prefix bytes and Redwood serves a cached response for the entire prompt+completion, billed tokens can be reduced.
   - KV-cache reuse in streaming/continuation: for long-running sessions where we reuse KV cache across tokens for the same session, we avoid re-encoding prefix tokens at each step.

Important: caching does not magically reduce the token count for entirely new user inputs — it helps when you have repeated prefixes or repeated completions that our cache hits. Cache hit rates are workload-dependent.

3) Target $/1M: our standard hosted pricing tier for models similar to what we demoed is $8 per 1M tokens (this is a placeholder rate for qualification; final quote depends on model variant & commitment). Using $8 per 1M:
   - 120M tokens/month x $8 = $960/month (gross)

Worked example with caching: if your workload achieves a 30% cache-hit on token volume (meaning we avoid sending 30% of prompt tokens due to repeated prefixes or cached completions), billed tokens drop to ~84M tokens, which would be ~$672/month at $8 per 1M.

Next steps I recommend:
- Aditya: can you share the lightweight instrumentation snippet (request headers + cache-hit tag) for the tech spike?
- Neha: can you prepare a preliminary quote (line item: $/1M tokens, expected monthly cost at 120M, and a 3-month ramp discount if applicable)?
- Alexa: if you confirm the 120M estimate and whether you expect ~30% prefix reuse, we’ll produce a 1-page MSP-ready quote.

Below I’m pasting a short FAQ that might help answer immediate follow-ups.

—FAQ—
Q: Do streaming tokens count differently?
A: No — streaming still bills by tokens consumed. The visible stream is just how you receive output; billing is unchanged.

Q: Are attachments or responses included in token counts?
A: Attachments are not tokenized; any text you include in a prompt (or that's encoded into the model call) is what counts.

Q: How do you measure cache hit rate?
A: We emit a cache-hit header per request and a per-route dashboard metric you can review in the Console.

Markus Klein
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up on pricing metrics from today's call

Hi Alexa / Markus —

I wanted to add a few practical notes from finance/pricing ops side that often come up during procurement reviews:

- Estimation vs billing: procurement teams often ask for character-based estimates because characters are easier to count on sample exports. We provide a conversion guide (chars -> tokens) but we always bill tokens. For your spike, send us a 24-48 hour sample of logs (anonymized) and we’ll run a tokensize conversion to give a more accurate monthly projection.

- Typical cache guidance: in conversational consumer apps with standard system prompts, we see 20–40% effective reduction in billed tokens from prefix caching. For transactional flows with highly variable user input, cache benefits are lower.

- Discounts & commitment: for ARR-aligned commitments we can offer step-downs: example — 5% off at $10k/month committed, 12% off at $25k/month, etc. Since your initial procurement target is <$3k/month, most of the discounts are triggered after you grow past the reserved tiers. We can include a promotional canary discount for the first 2 months if that helps procurement signoff.

Aditya — I’ll need a short summary table from you (Model variant / baseline $/1M / projected discounted $/1M for 120M) so we can draft a formal quote. Markus — happy to be on the procurement call if helpful.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Pricing & Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Thanks Markus / Neha — this is super helpful. A couple quick confirmations and asks: 

- We’ll run a 48-hour spike next Tue–Wed and share anonymized logs. Expect ~120M projected monthly tokens based on our sampling. We’ll try to instrument for prefix tags so we can measure cache-hit ratio; if we get ~25–35% hit we'll share results.
- Procurement would like the $/1M line item in a simple CSV (baseline and promotional canary price). Can you have Aditya or Neha send that before EOD Friday?
- Also: can you confirm whether model quantization or switching to smaller model variants changes the billing unit? (i.e., if we serve a quantized model, is billing still by tokens and not by GPU-hours?)

If you can answer those three quickly we’ll move procurement forward. Happy to set a follow-up 15-min call if needed.

Appreciate it —
Alexa
